clue.text: Flatus mostly annoyed the Queen?

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the word for annoyed loses its final letter

parts.note: flatus is intestinal gas, politely called wind
sore can mean irritated or annoyed

explanation.surface: A cheeky picture of someone breaking wind and offending Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the Queen is defined by her family name rather than her title.
explanation.definitionFit: Windsor is the surname of the British royal house, so the late Queen Elizabeth II was a Windsor.

clue.text: Above topless excitement, eh? Yeah right!

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of a word is its first letter, so topless strips that letter away
in a down entry, putting one piece above another means it comes first in the answer

parts.note: an exclamation asking someone to repeat themselves
fever as in a fever of excitement

explanation.surface: A sarcastic retort to someone's overexcited nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads backwards in the clue: eh? sits above the shortened excitement, since this is a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive interjections expressing disbelief or indifference to what another person has just said.

clue.text: Clergyman snorting kilo up in the buff

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top
someone snorting a drug takes it inside, so the clergyman word takes in the letter for kilo

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric
K is the abbreviation for kilo

explanation.surface: A scandalous image of a churchman taking cocaine while naked.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in the buff is the idiom for wearing no clothes at all, completely unclothed.

clue.text: "One fleeces society to make out" — The Queen

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society
to make out a sound is to hear it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen

explanation.surface: A mock quotation from the monarch accusing someone of swindling society.
explanation.walkthrough: Fleeces looks like cheating, but here it means shearing a sheep's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A shearer is a worker who clips the wool coat off sheep, removing the animal's fleece.

clue.text: Go through boozy dessert, but skip the starter

indicators.note: skipping the starter of a meal means leaving out its first course, here the first letter

parts.note: trifle is a British pudding of sponge soaked in sherry, custard and cream

explanation.surface: Working through a sherry-laden pudding without eating any starter.
explanation.walkthrough: The dining surface hides that 'Go through' means search, as in rifling through a drawer.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle is to search hurriedly through drawers or belongings, often looking for something to steal.

clue.text: Worrier with trouble getting grass

parts.note: fuss is bother or trouble
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: An anxious person gets into bother over buying cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is someone who frets excessively over small details, a habitual worrier.

clue.text: Given form of Villa, ultimately I shed no tears

indicators.note: read as a verb, tears means rips apart, so the words before it are torn up and rearranged
ultimately points to the last letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the final letters of the two words
seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A stoic Aston Villa fan insists defeat brought no tears.
explanation.walkthrough: Tears looks like weeping but is the verb meaning rips. Villa is the football club Aston Villa.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashioned is the past participle of fashion, to shape or make, so something fashioned has been given form.

clue.text: Cross and weary after the Spanish turned up

indicators.note: after means the word for weary follows the other piece
in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: las is the Spanish feminine plural for the
to weary someone is to tire them

explanation.surface: Someone grumpy and exhausted after meeting some Spaniards.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross reads as angry alongside weary, but it is the noun, an X-shaped cross.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is a diagonal X-shaped cross in heraldry, as on the Scottish flag of St Andrew.

clue.text: Trite remark on freedom is claptrap ultimately

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end of the word claptrap, its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of claptrap
latitude is freedom of action or scope

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict that clichés about liberty are so much nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, the freedom word sits on, beneath, the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude is a banal, overused saying offered as if it were meaningful, a hackneyed comment.

clue.text: Wanting bit of meth, shake three times over

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the shaking word goes without that letter

parts.note: to tremble is to shake

indicators.note: a bit of the word meth is just its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of meth

explanation.surface: A user craving methamphetamine shakes violently, again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Treble means threefold, multiplied by three, so something trebled has tripled in size or amount.

clue.text: Joint gets up one's nose endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly asks for an end of the phrase's word to be removed, here its front end

parts.note: something that rankles irritates you, gets up your nose

explanation.surface: A cannabis joint whose smoke irritates someone's nostrils.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint suggests cannabis in this drug-themed puzzle, but it is the body joint; 'gets up one's nose' is British for annoys.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankle is the hinge in the body linking the foot to the leg, a typical bodily joint.

clue.text: Fluid drunk with ales? A volley of shots!

indicators.note: something drunk is staggering and disordered, so the letters lose their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Liquids downed alongside beers, then a round of shots in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: Shots looks like more drinks in the drinking scene, but they are gunshots.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusillade is a rapid series of gunshots fired together or in quick succession.

clue.text: Back aim to take heroin out of hospital

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim

indicators.note: out of here means without, so the drug word is left lacking the hospital letter

parts.note: horse is street slang for heroin
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A plan to smuggle heroin out of a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The heroin is not the letter H here but its slang name, and the abbreviation for hospital is what is removed from it.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a proposal or candidate is to support or approve it publicly, which is endorsing it.

clue.text: I fool Self to get a line and H for myself!

parts.note: taken as written
a nit is a silly person, short for nitwit
the self, the ego, is I
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to fooling themselves while writing a line.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is Hoskins, so H is what they would sign with.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial is the first letter of a name, and H begins the setter's pseudonym Hoskins.

clue.text: I wondered about retirement cover

indicators.note: about suggests turning things around and around, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pondering how to insure themselves for their pension years.
explanation.walkthrough: Retirement cover sounds like a pension or insurance, but retiring here means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilted bed covering filled with down, used when one retires for the night.

clue.text: Moaner due to get smacked for behaviour

indicators.note: being smacked knocks things about, so the letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A whiner about to be punished for their conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: Smacked also hints at smack, slang for heroin, fitting the drug-laden theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeanour is the outward manner or way a person conducts themselves, their bearing and conduct.

clue.text: Odious leader taking power to crush men?

definitions.text: Odious leader taking power to crush men?

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of odious

parts.note: the first letter of odious
P is the abbreviation for power
to press is to squeeze or crush
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A hateful ruler seizing control in order to grind down the populace.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a tyrant who takes power to crush people.
explanation.definitionFit: An oppressor is someone who uses authority to keep others down harshly, which a hateful leader crushing people does.

clue.text: Drug that's turned around problem animals

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: turned around means the following word is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A narcotic that has transformed troublesome creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless Australian birds, and birds are animals, so this is defined by category.

clue.text: When to get supplied with drugs of different classes

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
sorted is British slang for having obtained one's drugs

explanation.surface: Wondering when one will score a mix of Class A and B drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Classes evokes the UK drug classes A, B and C, but it simply means kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: Assorted means mixed, made up of various kinds or sorts, so the items belong to several categories.

clue.text: Naughty stuff is S&M — time you whipped back!

parts.note: the letters as written

indicators.note: whipped back suggests snapping round in the opposite direction, so the two pieces before it are read backwards

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
U is text-speak for you

explanation.surface: A kinky exchange: sadomasochism is filthy, so it's your turn to be whipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Smut is obscene or indecent material, the kind of rude content one might call naughty.

clue.text: Reportedly, they might be fans of Tees puzzles

indicators.note: reportedly means as said out loud, so we want a word that is pronounced like the description

parts.words: they might be fans of Tees
parts.note: people fond of the River Tees in north-east England, jokingly called Tees-ers

explanation.surface: Supporters of Teesside are into brainteasers.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tees is a river in north-east England; a made-up name for its fans sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is a tricky problem or brain-teaser, so the plural means difficult puzzles.

clue.text: Us pigs end up displaying this

definitions.text: Us pigs end up displaying this

indicators.note: ending up in a mess suggests the letters before it are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Greedy pigs confess that they finish up looking plump.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: what pigs end up showing is plumpness.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudginess is chubbiness or plumpness, the rounded fat body that well-fed pigs typically display.

clue.text: Quarantine one's behind if full of a little gas

indicators.note: being full of something means holding it inside, so the first phrase holds the gas letter

parts.note: one is roman numeral I, plus the 's
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen; a little signals an abbreviation
behind schedule means late

explanation.surface: A flatulent person told to stay away from others.
explanation.walkthrough: One's behind, read as 'one is late', gives the outer letters, which hold the gas letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarantine someone is to keep them apart from others to prevent infection, which is to isolate them.

clue.text: Drink with drink in it? Excellent!

indicators.note: having something in it means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: to sup is to drink
to lap is to drink as a cat does

explanation.surface: A cocktail with another drink inside it gets an enthusiastic thumbs up.
explanation.walkthrough: Slap-up is British informal for lavish, as in a slap-up meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap-up meal or celebration is lavish and first-rate, so the word describes something splendid or excellent.

clue.text: Something escaping Slash? Intros to all G'n'R EPs

parts.note: slash and leak are both British slang for urinating

indicators.note: an intro is the opening of a song, so the first letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the first letters of each word

explanation.surface: Guitarist Slash of Guns N' Roses introduces the band's EPs.
explanation.walkthrough: Slash looks like the Guns N' Roses guitarist, but it is slang for a pee.
explanation.definitionFit: Leakage is the act or amount of something escaping through a hole or crack, a leak.

clue.text: Group of stars almost get goal with good ball

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the scoring word drops its last letter

parts.note: to score is to get a goal
pi, short for pious, means good
O is the shape of a ball

explanation.surface: Star footballers nearly score from a well-placed pass.
explanation.walkthrough: Stars and ball suggest football, but the group of stars is a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorpio is a constellation of the zodiac, and a constellation is a named group of stars.

clue.text: I'm annoyed model nurses take too many drugs

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold something close, so the modelling word holds the overdose letters

parts.note: to sit is to pose as a model for an artist
OD is short for overdose

explanation.surface: An exasperated agent complains that their model has overdosed.
explanation.walkthrough: Model is a verb, to pose, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: Sod it is a mild British oath expressing frustration, the same feeling as saying you are annoyed.

clue.text: Bit quiet for those monitoring the airwaves?

indicators.note: people monitoring airwaves are listening, so what matters is how the word is heard

parts.note: peace is quiet, calm

explanation.surface: A short silence for radio listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a portion or fragment of something, just as a bit is a small part.

clue.text: Prosecuted over small bit of skunk? Go on!

indicators.note: the final phrase is placed over, covering, the small pieces, so it wraps them

parts.note: to proceed is to go on
S is the abbreviation for small

indicators.note: a bit of skunk is just the opening letter of that word

parts.note: the first letter of skunk, strong cannabis

explanation.surface: Someone charged for possessing a tiny amount of cannabis, urged to carry on.
explanation.walkthrough: Go on! reads as encouragement but supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, to process someone is to serve a summons or bring a legal action against them, to prosecute.

clue.text: Warning: beer leads to recall trouble

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

indicators.note: the leads of words are their front letters, so the first letter of each following word is taken

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A health warning that drinking causes memory problems.
explanation.definitionFit: An alert is a signal or notice of danger, so it serves as a warning to be careful.

clue.text: A drug addict one examines carefully

parts.note: a means per, as in fifty pence a pound
a user is someone who takes drugs

explanation.surface: A clinician scrutinises a drug addict.
explanation.definitionFit: A peruser is someone who reads or studies something thoroughly, scanning it in detail.

clue.text: Tory leader gone on heroin, E and baccy

indicators.note: in an across entry, gone on these pieces means the gone word follows them
the leader of a word is its first letter, here of Tory

parts.note: the first letter of Tory
H is slang for heroin
taken as written; E is also ecstasy
to have gone to the loo, to have wee'd

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician exposed taking heroin, ecstasy and tobacco.
explanation.walkthrough: Gone means relieved oneself, as in 'I've just gone'. Baccy is British slang for tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: The weed is an old jokey name for tobacco, smoked as a leafy plant, so it matches baccy.
